info.text:
Most states have no lemon law just for used cars.
About 10 states have used-car lemon laws, including New York and Massachusetts.
All 50 states cover new cars: in California, 4 repair tries (2 for safety defects) or 30+ days in the shop within 18 months/18,000 miles presumes a lemon.
A buyback isn't a full refund: California subtracts a usage offset (hypothetical: $2,500 on a $50,000 car first repaired at 6,000 miles).
Sources: CA Civil Code 1793.22, CT Office of Legislative Research, FTC.
News and education, not financial advice.

info.text: Every state has a lemon law for new cars, but only about 10 have one for used cars, per Connecticut's legislative research office (counts vary). California presumes a lemon after 4 repair tries (2 for safety defects) or 30+ days in the shop within 18 months or 18,000 miles, and buybacks subtract a usage offset. The federal Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act covers written warranties, per the FTC. News and education, not financial advice. #Shorts #lemonlaw #carbuying
